build.title: How we built it
build.line: Five people, their coding agents, one shared board.
build.method: In the product repo: git fetch origin; git rev-list --count origin/main (197); gh pr list --repo aaron-sulbaran/meta-MIUT --state merged --limit 500 --json number, counted the entries (131); git ls-tree -r --name-only origin/main | grep -c '\.test\.ts$' (64). Hub events: the hub stores one JSON file per action under events/<date>/, so find events -type f -name '*.json' | wc -l (1221). People: five, from the hub's team list.

questions.q: Why not just build this on Instagram?
questions.a: The events live on Facebook: found there, RSVPs there. Instagram is one way in, like a flyer photo or a spoken line. The goal is more young adults opening Facebook, so the product has to live there.

questions.q: Why would young adults use this?
questions.a: People our age open Facebook to get something out of it. Free food is the Events version of that. It changes daily: three picks for today, and an alert only when something free is close and you are free.

questions.q: Is the AI essential or decorative?
questions.a: Essential. Six moments in the skit were live calls to Meta's Muse models, each timed on screen. Without them nobody types events in, so there is nothing to show.

questions.q: What is real and what is staged in the demo?
questions.a: Every Muse answer is a live call, and a recorded one says so on screen. The Instagram, Reels and lock screen moments are staged, and so is the friend graph. We say which is which.

questions.q: How does it get events without extra work for organizers?
questions.a: An organizer shares a flyer photo or says one line. Muse drafts the event, shows where each field came from, and the organizer only approves. An Instagram post can feed the same draft.

questions.q: What about privacy, location and company?
questions.a: Both are off by default. Lisa turned on Open to company herself, and only then could Muse suggest her to someone new. Location stays opt in too. We plan per-person controls, not one rule for everyone.

questions.q: What would it take inside Facebook?
questions.a: Events already cross-posts from Instagram, so this extends it. It needs Muse reading the post, the Events tab ranking per student, and a nearby alert. We built each piece on the Muse API.

questions.q: Why not fine-tune a model for this?
questions.a: A mentor suggested it. We chose Muse for the core and added photo and voice input, visible evidence per field, and organizer approval. Fine-tuning on Facebook event posts is a good next step.
